medications.dose: 2.5 mg PO once daily, titrate every 2‑4 weeks to 5 mg then 10 mg as tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually; titration period 8‑12 weeks
medications.purpose: Treat stage 1 hypertension, provide renal protection and reduce cardiovascular risk
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181/PH46/NG28 recommend ACE‑I as first‑line antihypertensive in metabolic syndrome (target <140/90 mmHg)

medications.duration: Lifelong — lipid panel at 12 weeks then annually
medications.purpose: Reduce LDL‑C and overall cardiovascular risk
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181/PH46/NG28 advise statin therapy for LDL‑C >100 mg/dL or QRISK ≥10 %

medications.dose: 500 mg PO once daily with evening meal, increase by 500 mg weekly to 1 g BID (max 2 g/day)
medications.duration: Lifelong — HbA1c review at 3 months then 6‑monthly
medications.purpose: Improve insulin sensitivity and prevent progression to type 2 diabetes
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 recommends metformin as first‑line for high‑risk prediabetes (HbA1c 6.3 %) when eGFR ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m²

medications.duration: Lifelong — renal function review 2 weeks after start then annually
medications.purpose: Renal and cardiovascular protection; modest glucose‑lowering and weight loss
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG106/NG28 recommend SGLT2‑i for CKD/diabetes risk and for cardiovascular risk reduction in metabolic syndrome

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive blood‑pressure lowering and possible electrolyte shifts (hypokalaemia/hyponatraemia).
interactions_checked.action: Monitor BP and electrolytes after dose changes; consider stopping HCTZ once target BP achieved.

interactions_checked.interaction: Both reduce intravascular volume → risk of orthostatic hypotension, especially early in therapy.
interactions_checked.action: Counsel on slow position changes, ensure adequate hydration, check BP and renal function 1‑2 weeks after each titration.

interactions_checked.interaction: Combined glucose‑lowering may rarely precipitate euglycaemic DKA, particularly if volume‑depleted.
interactions_checked.action: Educate patient on DKA symptoms, advise not to withhold metformin during acute illness without medical advice, monitor ketones if symptomatic.

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided; assumed >60 mL/min/1.73 m² based on creatinine 1.3 mg/dL in a young adult male.
Baseline liver function tests not available; assumed normal for statin initiation.
Serum potassium not available; assumed ≤5.0 mmol/L before starting ACE‑I.
Urine albumin‑creatinine ratio not available; will be measured to guide renal protection.
QRISK score not calculated; assumed ≥10 % given multiple risk factors.
Allergy status to ACE‑I, statin, metformin, SGLT2‑i unknown; will confirm before prescribing.
treatment_summary: Initiate ACE‑I (ramipril) for hypertension and renal protection, start atorvastatin for dyslipidaemia, begin metformin MR and dapagliflozin to address insulin resistance, prediabetes and provide renal/CV benefit. Monitor BP, electrolytes, renal function, lipids and HbA1c per NICE schedules. Advise lifestyle changes (diet, exercise, weight loss) and arrange baseline labs and QRISK calculation. Hydrochlorothiazide may be stopped once target BP is achieved.
